title: WPMS/2397/2001 of HARENDRA PAL SINGH Vs STATE and ORS.

paras.text: IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL

Writ Petition No. 2397 (M/S) of 2001
Harender Pal Singh S/o Sri Jagjeet Singh -Petitioner
 Vs.
State of Uttaranchal and two others - Respondents
 Sri J.S. Bedi, Advocate for the petitioner
 Sri A.K. Bansal, Standing Counsel for the State/respondents.
Hon'ble B.S. Verma, J. (Oral)
 By means of this petition the petitioner has sought a writ, order
or direction for quashing the order dated 28-4-2001 passed by
Additional Commissioner (Judicial) Nainital, Annexure No.13 to the
writ petition as well as the order dated 18-3-2000 passed by
Prescribed Authority Annexure No. 10 to the writ petition, whereby
the land measuring 1.381 hectare was declared as surplus on the
ground that the land has become irrigated and also sought the
quashing of notice (Annexure No.4) issued by respondent No.3
Prescribed Authority to the tenure holder.
 Briefly stated the facts of the case according to petitioner are
that a notice U/S 10(2) of the Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings
Act, 1960 (hereinafter referred as 'the Act'), was issued on
22.10.1975 to the petitioner-tenure holder to show cause as to why the
land measuring 0.23 acre land be not declared surplus. The
Prescribed Authority by its order dated 6.1.1976 accepted the ceiling
notice and declared 0.23 acre land as surplus, copy of which has been
annexed as Annexure-3 to the writ petition. Thereafter the respondent
No.3-Prescribed Authority again issued another notice in July 1994
under the Act and the entire land shown in CLH Fom-3 in transfer
statement was shown as irrigated. The entitlement was shown for
11.300 hectare and 15.805 hectare land which was proposed to be
declared surplus. The petitioner has filed objection before the
Prescribed Authority. Sri Virendra Pal Singh, who according to
petitioner is his brother, for being impleaded as party and he was also
allowed to participate in the proceeding. Harpreet Singh and Gurpreet
Singh, both sons of Harendra Pal Singh (petitioner) and Harendra Pal

2
Singh, all the three persons filed their objections Annexure Nos. 8
and 9 to the writ petition.
 The Prescribed Authority after hearing the parties and
examining the record declared 1.38 hectare land as surplus after
treating it irrigated land.
 Aggrieved by the order of Prescribed Authority the petitioner
preferred appeal before the Commissioner Kumaun Nainital. The
State also filed appeal before the Commissioner Kumaun Nainital for
setting aside the order passed by the Prescribed Authority. The
learned Additional Commissioner after hearing both the parties set
aside the order passed by the Prescribed Authority and remanded the
matter to the Prescribed Authority.
 The Prescribed Authority vide order dated 18-3-2000 again
declared the 1.38 hectare land as surplus holding that the proceeding
under the Ceiling Act do not bar by the principle of resjudicata in
view of Section 38-B of U.P. Act No. 1 of 1961 which was introduced
with effect from 10-10-1976.
 The State has issued the subsequent notice U/S 29of the Act. In
view of Section 29 of the Act, the Prescribed Authority as well as the
Appellate Authority gave a finding that the proceeding initiated U/S
29 and not barred in view of Section 38-B of the Act. The Prescribed
Authority has held that all the sons are major, therefore their land
could not be clubbed with the land of tenure holder as well as the land
of brother Sri Virendra Pal Singh, but on the issue whether the land is
irrigated or unirrigated the Prescribed Authority has held that the land
is being irrigated by private source of irrigation and in view of the
statement of Lekhpal treated the land to be irrigated.
 The appellate authority has suggested in its order that the
Prescribed Authority ought to have framed five points for
determination-
(1) whether the ceiling proceeding is barred by the principle of res-judicata?
(2) Whether the tenure holder and the family members acquired the
land after 1976?.
(3) Whether the transfer made by the tenure holder is valid?.

3
(4) Whether the major sons of tenure holder can be included in the
family of the tenure holder?.
(5) Whether the land of tenure holder is irrigated or un-irrigated?.
The Prescribed Authority has already framed three points in its
order, i.e. point Nos. 1,4 and 5 above as indicated by the appellate
authority in its order.
 Feeling aggrieved by the order of appellate authority this writ
petition has been filed.
 The respondent State contested the writ petition by filing the
counter affidavit. The stand taken in the counter affidavit is that the
family of the tenure holder is a joint Hindu Family. The Tehsildar
Kasipur on 14.2.1994 sent a statement including the land of the
petitioner, the land in the name of his wife Smt. Satnam Kaur and
sons Harpreet Singh and Gurmeet Singh. The Prescribed Authority
after giving benefit of two adult sons treated the land in their hand as
27.105 hectare of irrigated land and out of total irrigated land 15.805
hectare was proposed to be declared as surplus but the Prescribed
Authority declared only 1.381 hectare land of Khasra No.10M of
Khata No. 135 as surplus. It is further alleged in the counter affidavit
that the petitioner had transferred the land in favour of his sons by
way of family settlement.
I have heard learned counsel for parties and perused the entire
record.
 Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner has
contended that the land which was acquired by the sons of the
petitioner has been acquired on 20-9-1986 by way of family
settlement. This fact is not disputed that their names were recorded
on the land vide order dated 30-12-1987 by Tehsildar Kashipur.
 After a perusal of the order of appellate court it is quite clear
that the appellate court has to decide whether the land is irrigated or
unirrigated. It is well settled that the appellate court can re-appreciate
the evidence and parties can also adduce evidence if necessary to
decide the controversy or the evidence which was not within their
knowledge at the time of trial by filing additional evidence, but in the
case at hand since the notice U/S 29 of the Act was issued by the
revenue authority and revenue authority is custodian of the record, it

4
was the duty of the revenue official who was doing pairwee on
behalf of State to have filed Khasa of relevant year 1378 to 1380 fasli
when the land was made irrigated by the tenure holder and so far as
Section 29(2) is concerned the notice can only be issued in that event
when the land which was unirrigated earlier and has become irrigated
from a State irrigation work later on. The appellate court did not
consider this aspect of the matter and has committed a manifest error
of law in holding that the learned Prescribed Authority has not
considered the evidence on this issue. The Prescribed Authority has
not considered the provision of Section 29(2) of the Act.
 In the case at hand no factual verification is required since it is
admitted in the statement of Lekhpal and in the finding given by the
Prescribed Authority that there is a private source of irrigation and if
the private source is there the land cannot be treated as irrigated U/S
29(2) of the Act. Therefore the finding of Prescribed Authority as
well as appellate authority on this issue is totally perverse and against
the facts on record.
 Learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of the
respondents has contended that in the Khasra of 1399, 1400, 1401
and 1402 Fasli source of irrigation as tube-well and boring has been
mentioned and these documents show that the land had irrigation
facilities and have rightly been treated as irrigated land.
These papers have been annexed with the counter affidavit, but
they are typed copies and no certified copies have been filed. Even
otherwise there is mention of tube-well and boring but there is no
mention that the tube-well and boring belong to State. This fact rather
supports the version of Lekhpal that there are private source of
irrigation. Therefore the finding of appellate court as well as
Prescribed Authority is perverse that the land is irrigated land.
 So far as the land which was acquired by sons of the petitioner
from their grandfather and from their father by way of family
settlement if the Prescribed Authority feels that they are having land
more than ceiling area, the authority may initiate proceeding at any
time subject to the condition that they are having more than ceiling
area. But that land has no relevance with the land of tenure
holder/petitioner. It is pertinent to mention here that in earlier round of

5
litigation the land was treated unirrigated with the surplus land of
0.23 acre and the notice was issued on the ground that subsequently
this land has become irrigated. Since the finding on the issue or
irrigation is perverse therefore the total land of tenure holder if treated
unirrigated in that event the family settlement does not affect the
tenure holder in any way.
 Learned standing Counsel also submitted that the appellate
court has remanded the matter to the Prescribed Authority and the
order of appellate court cannot be treated as has been passed on merit.
 This submission has also no substance. Since the appellate
court has already substituted his own finding after discussing all the
issues therefore it cannot be treated only a remand order since he has
decided the appeal on merit. It is significant to mention here that the
notice U/S 29(2) can only be issued to the tenure holder in case the
unirrigated land has become irrigated from a State irrgation work
lateron and not by a private source of irrigation . The concerned
Lekhpal has mentioned in his statement that private source of
irrigation is there thus the initiation of subsequent ceiling proceeding
against the tenure holder is bad in law and the notice Annexure No.4
is liable to be quashed.
In view of earlier order the land which was surplus has already
been handed over to the State government.
 For the reasons recorded above the impugned orders are liable
to be set aside.
 The writ petition is allowed. The impugned orders are set aside.
The notice Annexure No.4 issued under Rule 8 of the Act and
proceedings initiated are hereby quashed.
ISB (B.S. Verma, J.)
 06-12-2012
